incident-bot: ALERT: Canary rollout v3.2.0 -> p99 request latency spike detected in eu-west-1 canary pool. p99 jumped from 120ms to 2.1s. Error rate stable. Trigger: latency > 1s for 5m.
Anna K: seeing it on the dashboard — confirmed. canary traffic is ~7% of total.
Miguel R: rolling v3.2.0 the new batch-acceleration kernel? I pushed the canary at 21:03 UTC.
Lee Chen: yep that change. suspected change: continuous-batching tweak + kernel fallback path.
Sara P: any customer-facing impact? any 429s or 5xx?
Anna K: no 5xx spike in logs, but streaming stalls reported occasionally. p95 up to 480ms, p99 2.1s.
John M: two customers on dedicated capacity in eu-west-1 reported intermittent UI hangs. Customer-ops notified them; they're seeing ~5% of requests >3s.
Miguel R: pulling traces now. running flame graphs for a few slow traces.
Lee Chen: can you dump a sample trace id?
Miguel R: trace ids: trace-7a3d, trace-7a45, trace-7a8f. main stack shows long kernel spin in attention.kernel_qkv.
Anna K: mitigation options: (1) rollback canary to v3.1.9 (2) route canary -> lower-concurrency lanes (3) throttle canary traffic to 1%
Sara P: recommend rollback if customer impact >1% and p99 >1s for >10m. We're at 5m and customers complaining.
Lee Chen: rollback is fastest. I can trigger immediate rollback for canary group.
Miguel R: before rollback, try reducing request_batch_size to avoid kernel path? but rollback is simpler.
Anna K: do rollback. I'll notify execs and oncall paging.
incident-bot: @channel Incident created: INC-2145. Severity: Sev2. Pager duty alerted: oncall Anna K.
Anna K: rolling canary back to v3.1.9 now. command: `deploy rollback --group=canary --to=3.1.9 --region=eu-west-1`
Lee Chen: running rollback command. output: `Starting rollback... draining new pods -> replacing with 3.1.9 -> healthchecks passing`
Miguel R: I'm tailing slow traces during rollback. if p99 drops after second node replaced we'll confirm root cause.
Anna K: traffic reduced and old pods returning healthy. p95 now 180ms, p99 240ms.
John M: Customer A confirmed UI responsiveness returning. They saw median drop back under 200ms.
Sara P: can we mark customers impacted and estimated window? John, please collect list of session ids, times.
John M: posting customer impact note to ops: "eu-west-1: 21:03-21:18 UTC, approx 15 minutes, affected ~3% of requests for two dedicated customers and some hosted canary traffic"
Miguel R: pulled diffs between 3.2.0 and 3.1.9: main change is batching heuristics + new fused-attn kernel. suspect kernel fallback under certain sequence length distributions.
Lee Chen: also saw increased KV cache miss rate in the slow traces — maybe fused kernel and cache eviction interplay.
Anna K: action items: rollback complete, monitoring for 30m, create follow-up postmortem, assign eng-runtime to root cause.
Sara P: I'll open an incident review doc and invite runtime + infra + pm. Also need a customer incident summary for affected customers.
Miguel R: will gather traces, kernel logs, and perf profiles (perf + nvprof) and add to doc.
Lee Chen: propose a canary checklist update: add sequence-length distribution smoke test and KV-cache checker before fused kernel flip.
John M: handoff to EMEA oncall in 20m. tagging Veronica for next shift. @veronica (not present) get a heads up: rollback done, monitoring stable, follow-up required.
Anna K: paging next oncall: Veronica, you are up at 21:40 UTC. I'll stay online for handoff.
incident-bot: Paging: @Veronica (next oncall) scheduled handoff at 21:40 UTC for INC-2145.
Sara P: summary for postmortem: Canary rollout of v3.2.0 introduced batching+fused-kernel change -> under certain seq length distribution and cache miss patterns caused long kernel spin -> p99 spike and streaming stalls. Rollback to 3.1.9 resolved latency within ~10 minutes. Customer impact: limited but visible to two dedicated customers; communications sent.
Miguel R: adding mitigation proposals: (a) revert fused kernel flag until canary-level perf tests pass; (b) add seq-length smoke test to canary; (c) add hot-cache stress test in CI; (d) temporary kill-switch for fused kernel per-region.
Lee Chen: +1 on kill-switch. also add metric for kernel-fallback-count and kernel-spin-time.
Anna K: closing live mitigation: rollback done, monitoring green, incident downgraded to follow-up. Will update incident channel when postmortem doc ready.
John M: customers notified, CS ticket IDs: #34211, #34212.
Sara P: assigning owners: Miguel (root cause traces + perf), Lee (fix + kill-switch), Anna (postmortem), John (customer comms).
Anna K: handoff notes: leave runbook section "canary rollback steps" updated with exact rollback command and smoke-checks performed.
Miguel R: copying logs and trace artifacts to the incident doc: http://intranet/redwood/incidents/INC-2145/artifacts
Anna K: thanks team. ending live paging. :thumbsup:
